claims.text: ProductsController carries [Route("api/v1/products")] on the class; List(), marked [HttpGet] with no id, answers the bare collection URL; Get(int id), marked [HttpGet("{id:int}")], answers the item URL.

OrdersController carries [Route("api/v1/orders")]; Create [HttpPost] and List [Authorize][HttpGet] answer the collection URL (List returns only the signed-in customer's own orders); Get(int id) [HttpGet("{id:int}")] answers the item URL.

scripts/up.sh at stage-1 prints "The lab is up." when ready. GET /api/v1/products at localhost:8080 then returns 200 with a JSON array of every product; GET /api/v1/products/1 returns 200 with one product object. curl sends one request; -i adds the status line and headers.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang scripts/up.sh @ stage-1; stage-1 lab: curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/products and /api/v1/products/1

claims.text: By a common REST naming convention, a collection URL usually answers GET (list) and POST (create), and an item URL usually answers GET, PUT or PATCH, and DELETE; HTTP itself attaches no such restriction — it defines each method against whatever URL is the target.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics); REST resource-naming convention independent of any one framework

claims.text: OrdersController has a Cancel(int id) method marked [HttpPatch("{id:int}/cancel")], answering PATCH /api/v1/orders/{id}/cancel; it calls OrderService.CancelOrderAsync, which sets Status to "cancelled", saves, and sends an "order cancelled" notification.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang OrdersController.cs lines 40-46 + DonHang.Domain/OrderService.cs lines 29-38 at tag stage-1

claims.text: AuthController groups its endpoints under [Route("api/v1/auth")]; its one action, [HttpPost("login")], answers POST /api/v1/auth/login. At stage-1 every endpoint comes from a controller whose route starts with api/v1 (Program.cs maps only MapControllers()).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang DonHang.Api/Controllers/*.cs + Program.cs line 72 at tag stage-1

claims.text: The {id:int} route constraint matches whole numbers, including negatives, up to a 32-bit range; a value outside that range does not match the route.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, routing fundamentals (route-constraint reference table)

claims.text: In Đơn Hàng's design, the collection URL (/api/v1/orders) and an item URL under it (/api/v1/orders/1) name two different resources — one represents the whole set, the other a single order — not two spellings of one.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang ProductsController.cs and OrdersController.cs at tag stage-1, plus the curl results of claim 3

claims.text: Under this lesson's convention, an action segment after the item URL fits when the server carries out a named action with steps beyond storing what the client sent; when the client only sets a value (e.g. overwrites one field), a plain PATCH on the item URL is enough.
claims.source_hint: REST resource-naming convention; Đơn Hàng's PATCH /api/v1/orders/{id}/cancel at stage-1
